subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented limits plus plugin/workaround guidance?
rationale: Choosing default exclusions, protected backup contents, and size/progress behavior affects restore completeness and recovery guarantees, so automation should not pick the final policy while a linked PR is already under review.

options.title: Review native scope controls
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement after resolving conflicts, real large-state proof, protected-path semantics, and restore-critical defaults.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Require proof that current or replacement backup code completes or fails clearly on large state directories, then track smart/custom exclusions under the broader exclude-pattern issue.

options.title: Document core limits
options.body: If core should not own smart/custom exclusion policy, document the native backup limits and point users to plugin or external backup options for selective cloud-style backups.

recommendation.title: Review native scope controls
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement after resolving conflicts, real large-state proof, protected-path semantics, and restore-critical defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the current volatile backup reliability fix and is the strongest current routing signal for the product boundary decision.
